chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Paying sidemen versus Hampton, South American touring and being voodooed
summary: Mingus paid sidemen over $1,000 a week by the night while Hampton paid by the week; his illness and Katherine Dunham.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: There's no future in it. To play jazz, you've got to be foolish. You've got to not want money, you got to not want to pay your rent on time. Only guys that can afford jazz now is the white guys. Lionel Hampton, man, he's still paying his men in these days, man, $400 a week. I was paying my drummer over $1,000 a week. I was paying my sidemen $900 to $1,000 a week. Lionel Hampton is paying his men $400 a week. Wait a minute, man, I paid them by the night, concerts.
Yeah.
He pays them by the seven day period.
No matter what they do.
That's right. And I worked five nights, they got paid five nights pro rata. If I played seven nights, they'd make over $1,000. I didn't want to work like that. I

worked where you take off and visit, and see who you are. You might be in Spain and might want to see a bullfight. Lionel Hampton -- the reason I know is Sue was booking him in South America, where I've been already.
Yeah.
And the manager was used to me coming over and leisurely going through the town. Lionel said, no, I want to go from job to job, every night. Because he's paying them by the week.
Yeah.
How can you be so greedy? To not want to -- you can't know anything.
Yeah.
You can't see anything like that. You can't -- how are you going to appreciate South America going through it like that?
And going through it like that --
You got nervous, too, man. It's a hard trip, because something was wrong -- the airplane might be a little late, you miss you gig.

Yeah. And also, the way you go through it, that must have some effect on your composition when you're on, because you've had a chance to go through a town, like the memories or sounds come back to you.
It does, man.
That's why I can't understand why I'm sick, because I never worked too hard.
Yeah.
I think I've been voodoed.
By whom?
Katherine Dunham.
Why Katherine Dunham?
Because I took the voodoo (unintelligible).
When it fell out, she said, I'm going to turn your picture around to the wall.
